items.message:

The weather increases tide table values by 0.09 m. Total forecast tide is 6.00 metres Chart Datum (2.95 mAOD) at Littlehampton. Strong Southerly Force 7 wind. 

Waves could cause overtopping of the beach, affecting Climping Street Car Park. A small amount of water may then flow or be directed westwards along Mill Lane towards residential property in Climping Street. Tuesday's tide at 11:30 on 27/10/2026 is forecast to be 9 cm lower (2.86 mAOD).
We are closely monitoring the situation . We routinely check the condition of the beach at Climping.
Consider activating any flood protection products you may have. Access could be restricted. Take care if visiting Climping beach.
This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

items.message:

Flooding may affect low lying land and roads adjacent to the river from the Welsh border at Llawnt to Shrawardine, near Shrewsbury. Other locations that may be affected include Llanymynech, Maesbrook and Melverley. Roads between Maesbrook, Melverley and Pentre start to flood. River levels remain high in this area. Flood alert thresholds are currently not forecast to be reached in any other gauge locations within this area.

We are closely monitoring the situation.

Areas most at risk include the tidal River Avon from Sea Mills to Conham in Bristol and between the Avonmouth Bridge and Shirehampton Park including Pill and Shirehampton.

The second forecast high water is at 7:30 AM on Tuesday 27/10/2026 with a level of 7.37 mAODN which is 0.38 m above tide tables, with south westerly force 6 winds. 
We are closely monitoring the situation and will issue further Alerts or updates as necessary. 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 1:00PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

items.message: On Wednesday, no flooding is expected but tides are higher than usual. On Monday night and Tuesday, no flooding is expected. On Wednesday afternoon, the weather increases tide table values by 0.22 m. The total forecast tide is 5.23 metres Chart Datum (2.50 mAOD) at Portsmouth. Light Westerly Force 4 wind. Wednesday's tide at 00:45 on 29/10/2026 is forecast to be 47 cm lower (2.03 mAOD). We are liaising with emergency services and local authorities over flood defence gate closures around Portsmouth. Consider activating any flood protection products you may have.  This message will be updated by 06:00 PM on 27/10/2026.

items.description: Isolated low lying properties along the tidal River Waveney
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding. 
Weather conditions are expected to improve and no further flooding is expected.   
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.   
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

items.description: Mersey Estuary at Arpley Bridge, Warrington
items.message:
High tides are expected to cause flooding overnight. 
Flooding is expected from to 12:30 AM on 27 October 2026. 
Locations most affected will be parts of Chester Road, Arpley Road and underneath Arpley Railway Bridge. We anticipate the next high tide tomorrow afternoon, 27 October 2026, to meet the flood warning threshold. We are expecting higher than normal high tides over the next 2 days, and a result, we may issue further flood alerts and flood warnings. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Start acting on your flood plan if you have one.   
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: Cumbrian coastline at Barrow in Furness, between North and South Walney, Cavendish and Ramsden Docks
items.message:
High tides, strong winds and large waves are expected to cause flooding overnight. 
Flooding is expected from 22:30 on Monday 26/10/2026 to 01:30 on Tuesday 27/10/2026 . 
Locations most affected will be Barrow in Furness including West Shore Park, Biggar Bank Road, Tummer Hill Marshes, Rampside, Roa Island, Vickerstown, Cavendish and Ramsden Docks, Salthouse Mills and Roosecote Power Station 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Monitor local water levels and weather conditions.   
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.
